episodes.205340: An early September moisture surge resulted in the return of a more active weather pattern to Utah, including some isolated instances of flash flooding as well as a strong thunderstorm wind gust.
episodes.205463: An isolated early morning thunderstorm generated strong winds 5 miles south southeast of the town of Mina, causing a small metal shed to tip over.
episodes.205468: A weak disturbance rounded a ridge centered over the Rocky Mountains and Desert Southwest on September 9th. Along with increasing surface moisture, this resulted in the development of scattered showers and thunderstorms across central and eastern NM. One thunderstorm produced a severe wind gust of 63 mph at Tucumcari Municipal Airport as it moved through the site. Shower and thunderstorm activity slowly tapered off across central New Mexico overnight.
episodes.205556: A couple of rounds of strong thunderstorms moved from east to west across Apalachee Bay.  Strong wind gusts in excess of 34 knots were measured.
episodes.206316: A trough with an embedded disturbance aloft produced isolated showers and thunderstorms across the region. Increased monsoonal moisture from the Southwest U.S. created enough buoyancy to produce a few stronger thunderstorms. One severe storm produced severe winds in Southwest Montana.
episodes.206642: On the 8th, modest northwesterly flow aloft, including an embedded upper-level impulse, was present across the Southern Plains. This enhanced flow and lift contributed to scattered supercell thunderstorms from southern Kansas into portions of northern Oklahoma and the adjacent northeast Texas Panhandle. In addition to reports of large hail and isolated wind damage, a well-documented tornado occurred in northern Harper County, north of the community of Buffalo, Oklahoma.
episodes.206652: Persistent onshore (northeasterly) winds along the local coast for several days created a local nor'easter which produced gusty coastal winds around 40 mph at times, waves of showers and isolated storms, rough surf, frequent rip currents and coastal / tidal flooding impacts around high tides at the northeast Florida coast, Intracoastal Waterway and the St. Johns River basin.
episodes.207053: A mudslide occurred in Custer County on Bayhorse Creek Rd about 1 mile from the Bayhorse town site.
episodes.207119: Multiple supercell thunderstorms formed across the eastern Texas and Oklahoma Panhandles during the evening hours of September 8th. The overall environment was highly conducive for severe storm development, with hail as large as 3 to 3.5 inches in diameter being measured across portions of the eastern Panhandles. Due to the low level winds increasing after sunset, this allowed storms to have low level rotation which led to an increased threat for tornadoes throughout the rest of the evening. The severe thunderstorms tracked south across the eastern Texas Panhandle and Beaver county in the Oklahoma Panhandle and produced large to destructive hail and at least one known tornado. These storms were slow moving and also produced heavy rainfall that likely led to flash flooding, especially southeast of Perryton where multiple storms formed and tracked over the same location. Thunderstorm intensity diminished after midnight across the eastern Panhandles.
episodes.207120: On the evening of September 9th, a very subtle upper level system passed over the region, which allowed several thunderstorms to develop across the western to central Texas Panhandle. The atmosphere was strongly unstable for September standards, combined with moderate wind shear and high moisture content, and this proved to be conducive for storms to produce severe hail, winds, and localized flooding. A few severe wind gusts were observed with two of the strongest storms, the highest of which were 70 mph occurring at the NWS Amarillo office and another northeast of Palo Duro Canyon in Armstrong County. Most hail was sub-severe, but quarter sized hail was observed with a severe storm in Carson County.
episodes.207322: Scattered thunderstorms developed over East Central Colorado during the afternoon and evening.  Hail up to golfball size was reported at Burlington.  A nearly stationary thunderstorm south of Flagler produced a landspout tornado.
episodes.207405: A weak outflow boundary from morning storms helped trigger storm development. Enough CAPE and shear (3000 j/kg and 40 kts) were present to support strong supercellular development. These supercells were prolific hailers and two cells generated giant (3.5-4 inch) hail.
episodes.207572: Tropical moisture associated with a tropical wave and other trade wind perturbations, along with an upper-level trough resulted in the formation of strong showers and thunderstorms. These showers resulted in flooding, landslide and wind damage along portions of eastern, northern and western Puerto Rico.
episodes.207580: Thunderstorms developed over central Cherry County during the early evening hours of September 8th. This activity developed along a surface trough of low pressure and quickly grew upscale. As this activity tracked east from central into eastern Cherry County, it produced hail up to the size of golf balls and wind gusts measured at 65 MPH.
episodes.207714: Northwest flow over the area produced high based and windy thunderstorms.
episodes.207761: A stationary surface boundary over South Florida with influence from a deep mid and upper level trough over the eastern United States led to diurnal showers and thunderstorms which produced heavy rainfall on the 8th and 9th of September.
episodes.207780: A stationary surface boundary north of the area and a mid to upper level longwave trough provided additional support for diurnal showers and thunderstorms on the 9th of September.
